notes.title: Retiring Community Treasures & Treasure Marketability Changes
notes.notes:
As the application of gambling regulations to video games changes, and potential new legislation is introduced in jurisdictions around the world, we want to ensure that Depth is available for as many of our players as possible. As outlined in Depth's 2018 Roadmap we will be retiring the sale and trade of all treasures in one week. While free reward treasures will remain in Depth, to comply with all international laws treasures from any source will no longer be sold by us, nor marketable on the Steam Marketplace. Note that this change applies only to the treasures themselves, any skins which are unboxed will remain marketable for the foreseeable future. At this time, we have no plans to make skins from the Community Treasures available on the Depth Item Store, however this may be something we may look to exploring in the future to continue to support our content creators. In recent months about 12% of Depth's revenue has come from treasure sales, so while this is some money it is not a large enough amount that it will impact our update schedule or content patch sizes.

Edit: Added FAQ
Which treasures exactly will not be tradeable/marketable?
All Treasures - this includes the Community Treasures, Event Treasures, Quest Treasures, etc.

Will my skins remain tradeable/marketable?
Yes, all skins will remain tradeable/marketable. This includes skins obtained from treasures both past/future.

Is Depth going Free-to-Play?
We currently have no plans of going Free-to-Play. (This question seemed to come up a lot below.)

Are you turning off the Steam Marketplace?
No, we have no plans on turning off the Steam Marketplace. Only the treasures themselves will no longer be marketable. All the skins will remain on the market, and remain marketable.

notes.title: Old Bones Update
notes.notes:
Old Bones brings a brand new map to Blood & Gold - Temple, a new evolution for sharks, changes to diver health and treasure, a new consumable for divers, and more.

Check out the update website: http://www.depthgame.com/old-bones/

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531680429
New Map: Temple
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531676607
Built to worship the Aztec goddess of oceans, Chalchiuhtlicue, this now time-worn temple crumbled into the sea during the late-1800's. The temple hadn't been fully explored before it disappeared, with recent expeditions heading under to both preserve and excavate the site.

Serrated Teeth - Shred Puny Divers
Tearing flesh to shreds, this abso-bloody-lutely vicious evolution leaves bitten divers to slowly bleed until they reach a Medkit... or death.

StubbsCare - Free Medkits and Diver Health Bars
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531677839
There's good news and bad news. The bad news is, while you were napping a bunch of other salvage groups have found out about our target locales. The good news is, so far their expeditions have failed, and they've even left a few extra supplies on the bottom of the sea. Stubbs says there's a good number of Medkits down there now, in between the corpses.

You've also been given an upgraded HUD for sensing when your vital signs drop - you'd best watch that closely it and make use of those Medkits when necessary!

The Supply Kit - The Whole Kit And Caboodle
Captain Stubbs has been losing a lot of good divers recently, not that he cares. But it's been cutting into the volumes of treasure he's been able to recover - and that does concern him. He's paid off a Russian mercenary to smuggle in a bunch of ex-military Supply Kits, and is making them available to you. For a fee of course, they weren't free...

Old Bones Hammerhead Skin
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531677528
Despite the ravages of war on its ancient frame, this death defying beast has terrified locals into believing it was chosen by Aztec gods hundreds of years ago to protect the sea no matter the cost.

Fight With The Ferocity Of Tigermaul Weapon Skins
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531678347
Dressed to the teeth and inspired by the fearsome Tiger Shark. The Tigermaul weapon skins feature a two-toned body topped with dark stripes and blood-red slashes.

New Randomized Treasure System
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531678088
Do you know all the Depth maps like the back of your hand? Know exactly which pieces of treasure to swim to and in what order? The challenge has just been increased - with treasure now spawning randomly in maps. This makes the Sensor a particularly tempting option early-on for divers.

Expanded In-Game Shop For All Skins
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531679650
Depth's in-game store has been expanded with a new area for browsing and managing diver skins and weapon skins, as well as shark skins. Preview and apply skins that you have access to, see how unlockable skins are gained, and purchase paid skins all from within the game.

All new and future skins will be available only through the in-game store, and all old skins are now available through the in-game store.

Full patch notes here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/274940/discussions/0/481115363857608763/

notes.title: Fresh Blood Update
notes.notes:
Fresh Blood is Depth's latest free update adding two new playable divers Finn & Shelly, a Blood & Gold variant of Station, scopes, new diver upgrades, new evolutions and more!

Check out the update website: http://www.depthgame.com/fresh-blood/

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274290

New Divers: Shelly & Finn

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274564

Shelly: Lead scientist for the Specimen Program at the Aquatics Research Lab, Shelly specializes in cybernetic organisms and was responsible for the creation of Specimen 8. After Specimen 8's escape to open water, Shelly was tasked with recovery of the beast due to her intimate knowledge of its systems and capabilities.

Finn: An astute surgeon and well read marine biologist, Finn oversees all medical operations and upgrades within the Specimen Program. With considerable experience handling the beasts, Finn was the first choice to join Shelly in the recovery of Specimen 8 after its escape from the Aquatics Research Lab.

New Map: Station

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274710
An old disused pumping station, used to refine and filter natural crude oil lies forgotten. Rumored to be the home of Specimen 8, Shelly and Finn have done their best to guide Captain Stubbs and the rest of the crew to this location for a chance at recovery.

Scopes - Love at First Sight!

Coming in telescopic and night vision flavors, scopes are a brand new type of upgrade for the: ADS Rifle, APS Rifle, Spear Gun, and Harpoon!

SCOPE
- Attaches a telescopic sight, giving increased zoom and reduced weapon spread when aiming down sight.
- Applies to the following weapons: APS Rifle, ADS Rifle, Spear Gun, Harpoon

NIGHT VISION SCOPE
- Attaches a night vision scope, giving increased zoom, reduced weapon spread, and better visibility when aiming down sight.
- Applies to the following weapons: APS Rifle, ADS Rifle, Spear Gun, Harpoon

New Diver Upgrades!

SONAR
- Fit with a sonar-based tracking device, these spears briefly reveal sharks they pass by.
- Applies to the following weapons: Spear Gun, Spear Pistol, Harpoon

EXTRA MAGS
- Increases the total number of magazines carried, perfect for any trigger-happy diver.
- Applies to the following weapons: APS Rifle, ADS Rifle

New Shark Evolutions!

VITALIZED FRENZY
Killing a diver vitalizes the shark, immediately resetting the cooldown of its active ability.

KILLER INSTINCT
Satiated by the taste of any blood, evolutions that trigger on diver kills now also trigger after seal kills.

Long-awaited Skins for the Thresher and Great White

THESE SKINS ARE ONLY PURCHASABLE THROUGH THE NEW IN-GAME STORE.
ON SALE FOR 20% OFF UNTIL SEPTEMBER 14TH 2015

SPECIMEN 8 GREAT WHITE

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274631
For years the military has been searching for a way to gain an edge in aquatic warfare. It started with training dolphins... but that wasn't enough. Deep in an ocean laboratory at an undisclosed location, they have taken it to the next level. Unfortunately their creation managed to chew through a titanium fence, slaughter its handlers, and escape to open water. This is going to be one heck of a cover-up...

THORNTAIL THRESHER

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274472
If there is a lucky shark somewhere in the ocean, this isn't it. He has been poked, punctured, and lacerated by almost every type of flotsam you could hope to find at sea. The collection of splinters lodged in his tail have earned him a deadly reputation among divers who have been shredded by his prickly appendage.

IN-GAME SHOP FOR SKINS

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274361
Depth's main menu has been expanded with a new area for browsing and managing skins. Preview and apply skins that you have access to, see how unlockable skins are gained, and purchase paid skins all from within the game.

All new and future skins will be available only through the in-game store, and all old skins are now available through the in-game store.

notes.title: Hide and Seek Update!
notes.notes:
Click here to go to the update website!

New Game Mode: Hide & Seek

With this update we're adding a new game mode, Hide and Seek. One player starts as a shark, and must hunt down the divers. When a diver is killed they join the shark side, and killing all divers secures a win for the sharks. But beware - diver players can defend themselves with their Bang Stick!

Hide and Seek is launching with five maps - including versions of Fractured and Galleon, as well as new maps Wreck and Station. We've also included a new community made Hide and Seek map from Gameo, called Mausoleum. You'll find Hide and Seek under the Private Match section of the Play menus.

New Map: Stash

Just off the coast of Cuba lies an abandoned and forgotten submarine base. With its roots tied to the cold war era and hints pointing to a nuclear involvement this relic is said to hold stashes of cached weapons that could bring a pretty price to the right buyers.

New S.T.E.V.E. Weapon Skin Pack

http://store.steampowered.com/app/384240/

Alongside this update we're releasing the new S.T.E.V.E. Weapon Skin Pack, on sale for 20% off until July 12th, 2015! Fight with the style of the divers' robotic overlord S.T.E.V.E! The S.T.E.V.E. Weapon Skin pack adds new finishes for the SPP-1 Pistol, ADS Rifle, Sea Mine, and LJ-10 Volleyjet.

Note: Skins will not be available for use in-game until patch releases

Changelog:
This includes the major changes since the last update (minor bugfixes and changes are not included) 

Mechanics

Fixed bug where the sensor was awarding points to the diver when 'detecting' a stealthed Tiger shark.


UI

Bot Match is now renamed to Private Match.
Fixed bug where the in game scoreboard was not correctly handling dead players.
Improved UI visuals when switching between diver gear skins and diver gear categories.


Maps

Added new map Stash.
Quarry's safes now award $1000 from $500.
Cove: First Safes up from $1000 to $1300

notes.title: Progress Update! - Content Patch 2
notes.notes:
It's been a while since we showed any progress, and we feel bad for leaving you in the dark like that. Tons of stuff is going on behind the scenes right now, and we figured we owe you an explanation as to why things are taking so long!

So, for starters, we wound up overshooting the goals we outlined in our Q1 2015 Roadmap. When we started working on that content, we quickly realized that it could tie in to some new gameplay opportunities that would require more work, but could open up some seriously cool new mechanics in Depth. Well, we got a little ahead of ourselves and probably bit off more than we could chew. But we're finally getting close to finishing now, so the time is right to shed some light on what we have been up to 

STEVE Damage & Repair

STEVE is a pretty crucial part of game, for both teams. He sets the pace of the divers progress, and contributes significantly to their chances of winning or losing the match. The problem is that while sharks can damage and disable STEVE quite easily, destroying him is very difficult. This was a deliberate choice on our part because we ran out of time to fully flesh out STEVE's health and damage system and felt that making him super tanky would get around the problem. And it does... kind of. But we really wished that we could come up with more interesting mechanics that would make divers truly care about protecting STEVE from sharks, and would open up new tactics for sharks that involve trying to take STEVE out of the game completely.

To this end, we have re-balanced the way sharks deal damage to STEVE:

STEVE no longer takes 'stacking' damage from sharks
STEVE takes a fixed damage amount based on the size of the shark hitting him. Larger sharks hit harder.
STEVE no longer regenerates health on his own.
The more damaged STEVE is, the slower he moves.
As a result of these changes, STEVE is quite a bit more vulnerable to sustained ram attacks from sharks. To counter this, we have created a new diver item that allows divers to make repairs to STEVE on the go - "The Welding Torch".  It's quite affordable, and support focused divers should be able to keep STEVE in tip top condition if they choose to purchase it.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406877277 
Oh, and in case you were wondering - the welding torch is separate from the new diver gear we promised in the 2015 road-map. Expect more diver gear to follow!

UI Redesign

We're taking the opportunity to both refresh the look of Depth's menus, as well as expand and improve what the menus do. As an example, the diver spawn menu in Depth saw many revisions before launch, ending up with the current layout:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406888770 
This layout has some limitations:
Inefficient use of the screen space (see the top-right)
An intimidating wall of icons for buying weapons
New players don't see progression-locked weapons (so the game looks content-light)
Adding many more weapon choices will run us out of screen space

We've iterated a lot on both the visual style and the flow of the menus, winding up with something more like this:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406889392The whole screen space is used
Weapons are broken up by category
We're able to show progression-locked weapons to new players

But beyond fixing the limitations of the old menu, the new menus give us some cool new features, some of which become clear in the new weapon details screen:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406889422  
Weapon Upgrades! You're going to have a lot more options for how to tweak your loadout with the new content patch. And the number of weapons and upgrades the new menus will comfortably support is huge. On top of that, there's more information on weapons shown, and choosing skins for weapons is better supported. For example: With the new menu system you could add tagging rounds to a P11, or Tranquilizing rounds to your SPP1!

Leaderboards

An updated version of Depth's leaderboards will be rolling out with the update to address the issue of scores being reset undesirably, along with some new changes :

All Leaderboards will be seeded with the scores from all previous months. Almost all reset scores will be included thanks to regular backups
All Leaderboards will be made lifetime, and no longer reset monthly
All Leaderboards will be made Crown Eligible, if you are in the Top 10 on any leaderboard you will be seen with a dazzling crown in-game

AI Updates
Another area that wasn't on the roadmap but we felt strongly needed some love was our bot AI. AI for both sharks and divers have received updates for interacting with more elements of gameplay including:

Shark AI responding to Shark Shields and no longer attacking hidden targets without first getting close to them
Shark AI will attack STEVE when opportunity arises
Shark AI will go for seals when low on HP
Diver AI will place both Shark Shields and Sonar Buoys

Shark Species Abilities

When we started working on the new shark evolutions we promised in the roadmap, we felt like it would be a lot more interesting if instead of just adding a handful of generic evolutions, we instead added some that were unique to each of the shark species. We quickly realized that this wasn't going to work in the context of the current evolution economy. How could players 'buy' something that we wanted them to have from the beginning? Should we just make it super expensive? What about really cheap? After a great deal of back and forth we settled on the idea of adding 'abilities' instead of 'evolutions'.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406873872

Each shark species (Tiger, Mako, Great White) will now have its own built-in ability that does not need to be purchased to use. However, this ability can be improved by spending evolution points on it. We are still working out the finer details but as an example, we present to you the Tiger's ability which we call 'Adaptive Hide'. It applies a temporary camouflage effect to the tiger's skin that allows it to slip in and out of combat without being detected by sonar buoys or flares. (it also makes you somewhat harder to spot by divers, too of course!) Unlike evolutions, which are largely 'passive', these abilities are player activated, so you can use them whenever you feel the time is right!

We are very excited about these new abilities as we think they will add a whole new level of 'Depth' (OK, that one's getting old now) to the shark game.


New Map!

And If none of that convinced you that we've been working our butts off on this update, then I hope these shots of our new map will!
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406891930  
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406891872  
We will be revealing more details about the map and the rest of the content in the upcoming update in the next few weeks, scout's honor!

Finally, we would like to thank all of you for playing Depth and having faith in our promise to provide continued support for the game.  Our goal is to do more than just add new content.  We would also like to refine what content and mechanics are there, and improve every aspect of the game.  Your feedback is a huge part of this, so please let us know what you think of our changes and what you would like to see tweaked or improved in the future! ːgreatwhiteː

STEVE takes a fixed damage amount based on the size of the shark hitting him. Larger sharks hit harder.
STEVE no longer regenerates health on his own.
The more damaged STEVE is, the slower he moves.
As a result of these changes, STEVE is quite a bit more vulnerable to sustained ram attacks from sharks. To counter this, we have created a new diver item that allows divers to make repairs to STEVE on the go - "The Welding Torch".  It's quite affordable, and support focused divers should be able to keep STEVE in tip top condition if they choose to purchase it.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406877277 
Oh, and in case you were wondering - the welding torch is separate from the new diver gear we promised in the 2015 road-map. Expect more diver gear to follow!

UI Redesign

We're taking the opportunity to both refresh the look of Depth's menus, as well as expand and improve what the menus do. As an example, the diver spawn menu in Depth saw many revisions before launch, ending up with the current layout:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406888770 
This layout has some limitations:
Inefficient use of the screen space (see the top-right)
An intimidating wall of icons for buying weapons
New players don't see progression-locked weapons (so the game looks content-light)
Adding many more weapon choices will run us out of screen space

We've iterated a lot on both the visual style and the flow of the menus, winding up with something more like this:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406889392The whole screen space is used
Weapons are broken up by category
We're able to show progression-locked weapons to new players

But beyond fixing the limitations of the old menu, the new menus give us some cool new features, some of which become clear in the new weapon details screen:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406889422  
Weapon Upgrades! You're going to have a lot more options for how to tweak your loadout with the new content patch. And the number of weapons and upgrades the new menus will comfortably support is huge. On top of that, there's more information on weapons shown, and choosing skins for weapons is better supported. For example: With the new menu system you could add tagging rounds to a P11, or Tranquilizing rounds to your SPP1!

Leaderboards

An updated version of Depth's leaderboards will be rolling out with the update to address the issue of scores being reset undesirably, along with some new changes :

All Leaderboards will be seeded with the scores from all previous months. Almost all reset scores will be included thanks to regular backups
All Leaderboards will be made lifetime, and no longer reset monthly
All Leaderboards will be made Crown Eligible, if you are in the Top 10 on any leaderboard you will be seen with a dazzling crown in-game

AI Updates
Another area that wasn't on the roadmap but we felt strongly needed some love was our bot AI. AI for both sharks and divers have received updates for interacting with more elements of gameplay including:

Shark AI responding to Shark Shields and no longer attacking hidden targets without first getting close to them
Shark AI will attack STEVE when opportunity arises
Shark AI will go for seals when low on HP
Diver AI will place both Shark Shields and Sonar Buoys

Shark Species Abilities

When we started working on the new shark evolutions we promised in the roadmap, we felt like it would be a lot more interesting if instead of just adding a handful of generic evolutions, we instead added some that were unique to each of the shark species. We quickly realized that this wasn't going to work in the context of the current evolution economy. How could players 'buy' something that we wanted them to have from the beginning? Should we just make it super expensive? What about really cheap? After a great deal of back and forth we settled on the idea of adding 'abilities' instead of 'evolutions'.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406873872

Each shark species (Tiger, Mako, Great White) will now have its own built-in ability that does not need to be purchased to use. However, this ability can be improved by spending evolution points on it. We are still working out the finer details but as an example, we present to you the Tiger's ability which we call 'Adaptive Hide'. It applies a temporary camouflage effect to the tiger's skin that allows it to slip in and out of combat without being detected by sonar buoys or flares. (it also makes you somewhat harder to spot by divers, too of course!) Unlike evolutions, which are largely 'passive', these abilities are player activated, so you can use them whenever you feel the time is right!

We are very excited about these new abilities as we think they will add a whole new level of 'Depth' (OK, that one's getting old now) to the shark game.


New Map!

And If none of that convinced you that we've been working our butts off on this update, then I hope these shots of our new map will!
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406891930  
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406891872  
We will be revealing more details about the map and the rest of the content in the upcoming update in the next few weeks, scout's honor!

Finally, we would like to thank all of you for playing Depth and having faith in our promise to provide continued support for the game.  Our goal is to do more than just add new content.  We would also like to refine what content and mechanics are there, and improve every aspect of the game.  Your feedback is a huge part of this, so please let us know what you think of our changes and what you would like to see tweaked or improved in the future! :greatwhite:

notes.title: The Big Catch Update
notes.notes:
The Big Catch is a brand new free update for Depth bringing: the Megalodon Hunt game mode, two new playable sharks, The Tiger and Mako, a new map and more. Reel it in today!

New Game Mode: Megalodon Hunt
Megalodon Hunt is an all-new game mode for Depth. Five divers face off against the greatest and most ferocious shark conceivable - the powerful Megalodon. Megalodon Hunt is void of S.T.E.V.E. and instead of focusing on room-to-room combat concentrates on map-wide chaos. Divers scramble for treasure as the Megalodon puts up a relentless fight, however as divers get stronger the tables turn and the hunter becomes hunted. 

New Map: Devil's Head
Devil's Head – A flourishing gold mine turned abandoned shark haven. With three floors of winding tunnels and large excavated rooms, Devil's Head focuses on indoor combat within its flooded halls. Vertical exploration is a huge part of Devil's Head - as S.T.E.V.E. and the divers wind deeper in the mine, the sharks come and go as they please using deserted elevator shafts and busting through aged wooden structures. Divers and Sharks alike will be sure to find themselves adapting and working together within this sunken quarry! 

New Shark: Mako
The Mako may be the smallest of the trio, but don't let that trick you; he's fast as hell and twice as mean. With a sleek but fragile frame the Mako is built for speed and agility. With great finesse and carefully aimed attacks the Mako excels in one-on-one combat. Using his smaller frame to slip in and out of rooms, divers are sure to keep on their toes as he whisks their allies into the dark. 

New Shark: Tiger
The Tiger is a real man eater, and his striped hide makes him hard to spot. With a solid build and powerful muscles, the Tiger is adaptable to a wide variety of strategies ranging from hit-and-run to all out aggression. Putting his bulky framework to use means the Tiger is more than capable of taking a few bullets before making a lively escape. 

Rebalanced Great White
The Great White is as large as he is dangerous. With the introduction of shark classes we've reworked the Great White into a close quarters powerhouse taking full advantage of his enormous size. Being both slow moving and hard hitting the Great White will continue his onslaught as bullets and spears sail his way. 

New Gear: Shark Shield
Sharks are darn good at sensing but why let them! Utilizing a wide range of electro-magnetic frequencies the Shark Shield will disrupt the senses of any shark as long as it's powered on and make any diver inside its effective area undetectable. However with portability comes fragility, any shark that gives it a good ram should send it flying away in pieces. 

Depth Ed
We'll be reeling in DepthED with the Big Catch Update for those of you looking to dive deeper into Depth. This is a full suite of editing tools that allows players to create their own maps and mods for the game. If you'd like to know more and talk about the Depth Editor join us on our Steam Forums – Mapping and Modding subforum. We can't wait to sink our teeth into what you guys release.

We've added nine new achievements to the Blood & Gold game mode and four new achievements for the Megalodon Hunt game mode.

notes.title: Depth Beta Update: Final Beta!
notes.notes:
A big thank-you to everybody who has played Depth during the beta period. We've received a lot of useful feedback, and have been able to make a number of improvements based on it. Our focus in this patch has been performance and polish.

Performance

We've made numerous optimizations to Depth since the last update. Some small, some quite large. Their impact on your experience will vary a lot, but we're confident that everybody should get at least a 10% boost in framerate. Some hardware configurations will get much larger (even as much as 100%) boosts.

Map Balance

We've been watching carefully how the maps have been playing out in beta, and have made a lot of small tweaks based on both metrics that we record, and feedback from the community.

Some breakables have been added to areas in some maps to slow things down, giving divers a bit more time to set up around safes. We've also done a lot of work on treasure in the maps, with some maps seeing re-distribution to smooth out bumps in diver economy, and all maps getting tweaks to stop unreachable treasure.

Changelog:
This includes the major changes since the last update (minor bugfixes and changes are not included) 

Mechanics


Beached as divers now die when they land


Balance


Diver spawn protection time increased to 6s from 3s
S.T.E.V.E now drops a max of 3 treasure per ram
S.T.E.V.E now takes stacking damage from sharks
S.T.E.V.E now keeps moving without divers
Increased DPV speed and acceleration by about 20%
Increased APS Damage to 34 from 30
Increased ADS Damage to 29 from 25
Easy diver bots shoot slower


UI


Friend requests now show at the bottom of the friends list rather than the top
Now showing a hint to players when they can throw treasure at STEVE
Fix for crosshair appearing on non-crosshair weapons if they were your first weapon
HUD Info text shows again (appears with in-game scoreboard)
MVP award no longer given out to bots
Multi-kills fixed
Stopped rare bug where spawn menus would re-select previous game items even when you couldn't afford them


Maps


Fixes to Fractured to stop players from being able to exit the map
Lots of collision work to help map-falling, snagging, and getting stuck
Fixed pump god-spot in Crude
Treasure pass on all maps to ensure all treasure can be grabbed
Breakables added to 1st safe room in Crude and Fractured
Breakables added to 1st and 3rd safe rooms in Cove and Antiguo


Matchmaking


Improved reliability of lobby match joining


Content


Fixed the orientation of the trail on spear projectiles
Added a minor parallax effect to the diver's first person weapons (noticeable when the camera turns)
Added animations for deploying and idling with Sonar Buoys and Sea Mines
Falling players will cause a splash effect when they hit water
Added chain dropping and idle animations to Sonar Buoys and Sea Mines
Sonar Buoys now expire and shutdown when the battery runs out rather than just disappear
Sonar Buoys and Sea Mines now respond to being touched by pawns


Sound


Third-person sound added for the sensor
Fixed light and heavy weapon impact sounds being the wrong way around
Shutdown/destruction sounds added to Sonar Buoy


Steam


Leaderboards will now write in a 6-player game even if somebody disconnects part-way through
Achievements can't be gained against passive/easy bots anymore
Rich presence queuing and connecting should now work for lobby members


Other


Translations brought up-to-date
Players that leave a game are now replaced with a bot, so the game can continue
Game pausing disabled

notes.title: Depth Beta Update: Sounds, Languages, and Lobbies!
notes.notes:
It's been a while - and this is a big patch. A few major features have been in the works for months, and have finally arrived!

Rebuilt Sounds and New Sound Engine

Our sound guys have been working on this for months, and it's finally here! Everything about sounds has been completely re-built - a new more powerful sound engine is in use, and the sounds themselves have had a lot of work done.

This means improved occlusion, positioning and levels. You can now hear bullets whizzing by your head, and gunshots can be heard at long range (even if they're quiet). With HDR sound support, explosions don't distort, and loud sounds cause tinnitus effects when they're too close.
